target.title: fix(tailscale): retry status json after serve startup
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes the transient `tailscale status --json` startup race in Tailscale Serve mode.

- retry only recognized daemon-readiness failures: local daemon connection errors and status probes terminated by the existing command timeout
- propagate missing binaries, permission failures, malformed JSON, and other permanent failures immediately
- retry the same detected Tailscale binary so fallback does not switch installations
- rebuild the branch from current `main` while preserving the latest Tailscale whois, Serve, and Funnel behavior

Closes #42798.

## Verification

- `node_modules/oxfmt/bin/oxfmt --check src/infra/tailscale.ts src/infra/tailscale.test.ts`
- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/tailscale.test.ts src/gateway/server-tailscale.test.ts` (53 tests passed)
- `git diff --check`
- `node_modules/.bin/tsx /private/tmp/tailscale-91553-refresh-live-proof.ts` (3/3 real Serve cycles passed)
- final GitHub head `5a6e0cbc38b255c8b1acbdd916fceea10fb5fc17`: mergeable against current `main`, two changed files only

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Gateway Tailscale Serve startup now survives a transient first `tailscale status --json` daemon-readiness timeout and recovers the real tailnet hostname, while permanent command and parsing failures are not retried.

Real environment tested: Final PR head `5a6e0cbc38b255c8b1acbdd916fceea10fb5fc17` runtime surface on macOS arm64 with Homebrew Tailscale `1.98.8`, a real authorized `tailscaled` userspace daemon, real Tailscale Serve, and DNS name `openclaw-pr-91553-refresh.tail8ed022.ts.net`. The live-tested workspace and final PR head have byte-identical blobs for the changed runtime file (`6e6a1ee058c1ef5d7346572fe4818542e57f0600`), its test file (`aa32fb50679324d3782623f2e6467e2d1108e109`), the Gateway caller, and `runExec`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: `node_modules/.bin/tsx /private/tmp/tailscale-91553-refresh-live-proof.ts`. The harness invoked the real `startGatewayTailscaleExposure({ tailscaleMode: "serve", port: 18789 })` path three times. In each cycle, the first real Homebrew `tailscale status --json` call used an unavailable daemon socket and hit the production 5-second `runExec` timeout; the retry used the authorized daemon socket, recovered the real DNS hostname, and then ran normal Serve cleanup.

Evidence after fix:
```json
{
  "environment": "macOS arm64 + Homebrew Tailscale 1.98.8 + real authorized tailscaled",
  "cycles": [
    {"cycle": 1, "firstStatusUsedUnavailableSocket": true, "statusAttempts": 2, "recoveredHostname": "openclaw-pr-91553-refresh.tail8ed022.ts.net", "serveEnabled": true, "cleanupCompleted": true},
    {"cycle": 2, "firstStatusUsedUnavailableSocket": true, "statusAttempts": 2, "recoveredHostname": "openclaw-pr-91553-refresh.tail8ed022.ts.net", "serveEnabled": true, "cleanupCompleted": true},
    {"cycle": 3, "firstStatusUsedUnavailableSocket": true, "statusAttempts": 2, "recoveredHostname": "openclaw-pr-91553-refresh.tail8ed022.ts.net", "serveEnabled": true, "cleanupCompleted": true}
  ]
}
```

Observed result after fix: All three real Serve cycles made exactly two status attempts, recovered the real tailnet DNS hostname after the first timeout, emitted no Serve warning, and completed cleanup. Focused tests additionally proved missing-binary and permission failures execute once and malformed JSON is not retried. The temporary proof node was logged out and its daemon stopped.

What was not tested: The Homebrew daemon ran in official userspace-networking mode rather than as a root launchd system daemon. The startup race was deterministically induced through an unavailable socket and the real production timeout rather than waiting for nondeterministic host load. Funnel mode and unrelated Gateway paths were not exercised.
